text:
Omar: Hey team — had to take a cash taxi from the airport at 2am because the ride-hail app kept failing and there were safety concerns. Driver didn't give a receipt, total was €42. Can I still get reimbursed?
Kelly (People Ops): Sorry that happened. We do prefer official receipts but we can make exceptions for safety/time-sensitive situations. Please submit via Expensify and attach: a short incident note (one sentence) describing why you paid cash, a photo of the taxi meter/receipt if available, a photo of the vehicle or driver's card (if you took one), and the card/transaction screen if you used an app. If none of that exists, a manager attestation email + your bank statement showing the cash withdrawal used to pay is usually acceptable.
Omar: I only have a blurry photo of the car and my cash withdrawal on the bank statement. No driver card.
Kelly (People Ops): That's fine. Upload the photo + bank statement and add a one-line justification in the expense comments: "2am airport taxi due to app failures and safety; paid cash." Then ping your manager to approve the attestation in the comments. Finance will manually review.
Jules (Manager): I saw Omar's message and I approve — he confirmed it was during a client travel window and left the terminal due to safety. Approving expense in the comments.
Finance-Bot: Reminder: category = Ground Transport -> "Emergency/no-receipt taxi". If supporting docs are sparse, finance may cap reimbursement to reasonable local taxi fares. Please include location and distance if known.
Omar: Thanks everyone — uploaded bank statement + car photo and forwarded Jules' approval. Will submit now.
Kelly (People Ops): Got it — we'll triage once it lands in the queue. If finance needs anything else we'll reach out. Tip: if you ever have to pay cash, try to get a quick photo of the driver's badge or take a screenshot of the ride-hail failure for extra context. Closing once processed. :white_check_mark:
